facts.fact: The Department of Basic Education's 2025/26 plan says SA-SAMS is policy-driven and therefore developed and maintained by the Department, with provinces supporting schools in using its latest versions; no date is given, so the document's date is used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The 2025/26 Annual Performance Plan names SA-SAMS: it carries indicator 4.2.3, the percentage of public schools using SA-SAMS for reporting, measured annually, and commits the EMIS Directorate over the medium term to modernise it into a web-enabled platform with the National Education Collaboration Trust while keeping the current system running; document's date used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The plan lists SA-SAMS modernisation among unfunded mandates, to be funded through partnerships or sponsorships and a request to provincial education departments through HEDCOM; it states no budget line for the system; document's date used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The plan's desired performance is that all public schools use SA-SAMS as the standard application to capture and record unit school administrative data, with no level named; the one level-specific use it describes is schools uploading General Education Certificate scores; document's date used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The plan says schools will upload General Education Certificate scores onto SA-SAMS, that term 4 schedules are extracted from it for those schools, and that data from schools is uploaded manually into SA-SAMS with possible capturing error; it describes the system as holding school-level data in school databases; document's date used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The plan defines indicator 4.2.3 as public schools reporting through SA-SAMS over all public schools, both reported by provinces, but the passages give no value; it states that the Western Cape does not collect source data through SA-SAMS and that some schools will not use it for reporting; document's date used.
facts.system: South African School Administration and Management System (SA-SAMS)

facts.fact: The Department says about 99.9% of functional ordinary schools, public and independent and of all levels (24,850 schools in 2024), had their databases uploaded on LURITS and the Provincial Data Warehouses as of July 2024; the share counts schools whose database was uploaded, not schools entering attendance or results, and is not given for primary schools alone.
facts.system: Learner Unit Record Information and Tracking System (LURITS)

facts.fact: The plan says LURITS, introduced in 2009 to track the movement of learners, gives the year a learner started Grade 1 and the grade the learner is now in, and that learner progression can be tracked from grade to grade with it; the 2024 upload covered 13,527,283 learners in ordinary public and independent schools.
facts.system: Learner Unit Record Information and Tracking System (LURITS)

facts.fact: The plan says the Department introduced LURITS in 2009 and that its Financial Planning, Information and Management Systems subprogramme maintains an integrated EMIS based on learner record information; document's date used.
facts.system: Learner Unit Record Information and Tracking System (LURITS)
